output.content:
**NVIDIA Data Center—Q1 FY2027 growth drivers, in the context of FY2026**

- NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached a record **$75.2 billion** in Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended April 26, 2026), growing **92% year over year** from **$39.1 billion** in Q1 FY2026 and **21% sequentially** from **$62.3 billion** in Q4 FY2026—an approximately **$12.9 billion** sequential increase. [[1]]

- The principal driver was the continuing **Blackwell system ramp**, particularly strong demand for the **GB300 NVL72** rack-scale platform among frontier-model builders and hyperscalers; NVIDIA characterized Blackwell’s deployment as the company’s fastest product ramp to date. [[2]]

- Growth was supported by an inflection in **inference demand**, with Blackwell systems rolling out across a wider customer base: hyperscalers, model developers, AI-cloud providers, and sovereign customers. [[2]]

- The value proposition extended beyond GPU performance: NVIDIA said GB300 delivered a **2.7x throughput improvement** and a **60% lower cost per token** versus the prior platform six months earlier, improving the economics of AI-factory deployments and encouraging larger-scale inference build-outs. [[2]]

- **Networking was an especially important incremental contributor.** Q1 FY2027 Data Center compute revenue was **$60.4 billion**, up **77% year over year** and **18% sequentially**, while networking revenue was **$14.8 billion**, up **199% year over year** and **35% sequentially**. [[1]]

- The networking acceleration reflected demand for AI-cluster interconnects, including **Spectrum-X Ethernet** and **InfiniBand**; NVIDIA said InfiniBand revenue rose more than fourfold year over year, driven by next-generation XDR deployments. [[2]]

- Under NVIDIA’s newly disclosed customer-market framework, **Hyperscale** generated **$38 billion**, about half of Data Center revenue, and grew **12% sequentially**, while **AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise (ACIE)** generated **$37 billion** and grew **31% sequentially**; within ACIE, AI-cloud revenue more than tripled year over year. [[2]]

- FY2026 established the base for this Q1 acceleration: in Q4 FY2026, Data Center revenue was already a record **$62.3 billion**, up **75% year over year** and **22% sequentially**, as Blackwell adoption broadened. [[3]]

- Therefore, the Q1 FY2027 result was not merely a continuation of FY2026 GPU demand: it represented a broader **rack-scale AI-factory cycle**, combining Blackwell/GB300 compute, rapidly growing networking content, hyperscaler deployments, and faster-growing AI-cloud/enterprise/industrial demand. [[2]]

- Looking forward from Q1, management guided Q2 FY2027 total revenue to **$91.0 billion ±2%**, said sequential growth would be driven primarily by Data Center, and continued to exclude China Data Center compute revenue from its outlook—suggesting the reported demand trajectory was being supported without assumed China compute sales. [[1, 2]]
